program_overview.title: Game Development Complete Masterclass
program_overview.tagline: Both engines the industry runs on: Unity and C# from 2D to 3D and game AI, then Unreal with C++, multiplayer, and a capstone you actually ship.
program_overview.description:
Game development is a craft with two centers of gravity, Unity with C# and Unreal with C++, and serious studios expect you to be deep in one and conversant in the other. This live online masterclass builds both in the right order: game design and complete 2D games first, because finished small games teach more than unfinished big ones, then 3D in Unity, advanced C#, game AI and real 3D projects, plus mobile and cross-platform shipping. Then the second engine: Unreal fundamentals, C++ for games, graphics programming and engine architecture, followed by multiplayer, the hardest and most requested skill in modern game work. A finale month ships a polished capstone game and sits the final exam.

The pace is honest: ten teaching months at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of practice, with two more in hand. Problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest.
what_makes_this_different: Finished games from month one: complete 2D games before 3D ambitions
Both industry engines: Unity/C# depth plus a real Unreal/C++ phase, in the order studios expect
Game AI and multiplayer taught properly, the two topics tutorials always skip
Craft over hype: no VR/AR tourism, no live-service fantasies, just shippable skill
An honest 10-month arc with 2 months in hand
Real assessment: weekly problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams and a final exam with a free retest

faqs.question: What does this game development course cover?
faqs.answer: Game design and complete 2D games in Unity with C# first, then 3D development, advanced C#, game AI, mobile and cross-platform shipping. Then the second engine: Unreal fundamentals, C++ game programming, graphics programming and engine architecture, followed by multiplayer networking through a working online prototype. A finale month ships a polished capstone game and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn game development properly?
faqs.answer: Ten months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with two more months in hand for learners who need them. The three teaching phases build the skill and its real-world application; the finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Unity or Unreal: which should I learn?
faqs.answer: Both, in the order this course teaches them. Unity with C# is the gentler engine to learn deeply and dominates mobile and indie work; Unreal with C++ carries AAA and high-end 3D. Studios increasingly expect depth in one and literacy in the other, which is exactly the profile this course builds: Unity depth first, then a real Unreal phase, and you graduate knowing which one fits each project.

faqs.question: Do I need a powerful computer?
faqs.answer: Not for most of the course: the 2D and 3D Unity phases run happily on ordinary laptops. The Unreal phase is where hardware starts to matter, a mid-range graphics card makes it comfortable, and we tell you the honest requirements before that phase begins so nothing surprises you. No phase requires a high-end machine.
